title: Request for UCR master files for years not on the Crime Data Explorer

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Request for UCR master files for years not on the Crime Data Explorer
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request copies of the following records of the Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) Program, CJIS Division:

The national master files for these collections, for every year the program holds before the first year the Crime Data Explorer (cde.ucr.cjis.gov) offers, as far back as the program's files go:
Return A (Offenses Known and Clearances by Arrest): every year before 1985
Supplement to Return A: every year before 1985
Age, Sex, and Race of Persons Arrested: every year before 1985
Arson: every year before 1985
Supplementary Homicide Reports: every year before 1985
Police Employee (LEOKA): every year before 1991 

For each year, the current version only; if identifying the current version would take more work than releasing every version the program holds, every version.
All documentation the program holds for those files: the record description (file layout) for each, and any other documentation, including coding manuals, code lists, records of changes to the files or their layouts, and notes that accompanied the files when they were distributed.
These are existing records: the program has distributed these master files to researchers before, on DVD.

Format. Electronic copies in the format the program keeps them, the fixed-width text master files, by download link or on a DVD or drive. No records need to be created or converted.

This request is for a noncommercial research project, not for commercial use. 

If any part of this request is denied, please release the rest, and cite the exemption for each part withheld.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jacob Kaplan

title: Chatham County Police Department: Vendors Paid, FY2026 and FY2027 to Date (Chatham County Police Department)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

A report or export from the County's financial system sufficient to show all vendors paid, or issued a purchase order, on behalf of the Chatham County Police Department for the most recently completed fiscal year (July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026) and for the current fiscal year (beginning July 1, 2026) through the date of this request. Please include the vendor name and, if the system maintains one, the vendor number. If the County's standard vendor or accounts-payable report already includes other fields, such as amounts paid, payment dates, purchase order numbers, or the department or cost center, please leave them in. I am not asking the County to create a new compilation.

This is a request for data fields in the County's financial database. Under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(f), please provide it in the format in which it is kept or in a standard export format such as a CSV or Excel file.

If these records are held by the County's Finance or Purchasing Department rather than the Police Department, please forward this request to the appropriate department and let me know where it was sent.

Under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(c)(1), any labor charge may not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid full-time employee with the necessary skill and training, and the agency must use the most economical means reasonably calculated to produce the records. I do not authorize any work that would exceed $25 until I have approved the estimate.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ethan Watters

1. Palm Beach Gardens Police Department. They hold the body camera footage, the 911 call, and the recorded interviews: Johnson’s confession, Elaine Simon’s interview and Kyle Bancroft’s statement at the scene. You request them through the city’s public records page by choosing “Request Police Records.” The city lists City Clerk Patricia Snider as its records custodian, at 10500 North Military Trail. The department sends files electronically, as a link emailed from Evidence.com, and body camera video is redacted under Florida statute. Expect a fee. Past requesters on MuckRock were charged $141.75 and $109.42 for other requests. Ask for the case number from March 12, 2018, at the BallenIsles home on Sunset Bay Lane. 
Public Records Requests

title: Obama Presidential Library: August 2016 CIA Courier Briefing to Rice/NSC re: Putin

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I. Subject Matter and Scope

I request all executive, national security, and administrative records originating from or maintained by the Office of the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs (Susan Rice) and/or the National Security Council (NSC) Secretariat between July 15, 2016, and September 30, 2016, inclusive.

This request targets all records — regardless of physical form — concerning, referencing, or summarizing the sensitive intelligence material delivered via courier (the "Eyes Only" or "Top Secret Envelope") from the Central Intelligence Agency to the White House regarding Russian President Vladimir Putin's direct role in directing the 2016 U.S. election interference campaign, as first publicly reported by Greg Miller in The Washington Post ("Obama's secret struggle to punish Putin for election interference," June 23, 2017), including the internal deliberations that preceded the October 7, 2016 joint DHS/ODNI public attribution statement.

For guidance, here is the article where the existence of the envelope is mentioned: 
https://www.washingtonpost.com/graphics/2017/world/national-security/obama-putin-election-hacking/

The scope includes, but is not limited to:

1. Internal emails, text communications, and electronic messages sent to or received by Ambassador Susan Rice, Deputy National Security Advisor Ben Rhodes, Deputy National Security Advisor Avril Haines, Chief of Staff Denis McDonough, or NSC staff regarding this intelligence.

2. "Night notes," daily briefing materials, cover memos, executive summary sheets, and intelligence routing slips accompanying or summarizing the CIA briefing packet.

3. Official meeting summaries, readouts, attendee logs, action-item tracking logs, and personal notes generated during or immediately following NSC Principals Committee or Deputies Committee deliberations on this material.

4. Any drafts, talking points, or option papers prepared for the President regarding potential responses to the reported Russian activity during this period.

5. Photographs of the actual top secret envelope itself. Specifically, this is a request for any photographs of either the sealed or opened envelope delivered to the White House taken in order to confirm receipt. 

III. Concurrent Mandatory Declassification Review Request

To the extent any responsive records are withheld in whole or in part on the basis of classification under FOIA Exemption (b)(1) or the corresponding PRA restriction category, I request that those records be concurrently referred for Mandatory Declassification Review pursuant to Executive Order 13526, Section 3.5, so that this review may proceed in parallel rather than sequentially.

IV. Public Interest Fee Waiver

Disclosure is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of government operations and is not primarily in my commercial interest. The processing of intelligence on 2016 foreign election interference remains a matter of substantial, ongoing public interest involving national security governance, executive decision-making, and historical accountability, and the requested records would be made publicly available through MuckRock News.

V. Expedited Processing

I request expedited processing pursuant to 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(E) given the sustained public and media interest in this subject matter and my role as an active member of the news media disseminating FOIA-obtained records on this topic.

VI. Format and Processing

Please produce all responsive records in electronic format (PDF) via email or secure file transfer. If any portions are withheld under a statutory or PRA exemption, release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions. For any records withheld in full or in part, provide a Vaughn index itemizing each withheld record or redaction and the specific statutory or PRA basis claimed. If any records are referred to the Central Intelligence Agency or another agency for consultation under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6) or 44 U.S.C. § 2208, please notify me of the referral and the referred agency's identity.

Thank you for the work that the Obama Presidential Library does every day.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware
